art.title: Mona Lisa
art.credit: Public domain · image via Wikimedia Commons (C2RMF)
art.story: Around 1503 Leonardo began a portrait of Lisa Gherardini, the wife of a Florentine silk merchant. He never handed it over: he kept working on it for years and took it with him to France. Her smile seems to come and go because Leonardo blurred the corners of her mouth and eyes into soft shadow, a smoky technique called sfumato. Behind her, a road and a river wind through strange blue hills. In 1911 the painting was stolen from the Louvre; its return two years later made it the most famous picture on earth.
